* DB layout changes in other clients (after TG proves out pruning)

excerpts.author: jgm
excerpts.content: I'd rather frame the debate in terms of two positives, rather than a positive and a negative.  Seems we can either have Ethereum with higher decentralisation (lower hardware requirements) or with better user experience  (increased gas limit).  Both have benefits, and it's a question of weighing one against the other.  And it is, of course, a non-linear relationship: it _may_ be possible to increase the gas limit while not significantly impacting decentralisation _up to a point_.  Answers to questions like "if there are more nodes in total, can each node have fewer peers (up to a limit, of course) without harming either the node or the network?"

I have a 4tb ssd since 2018, and it never was as cheap as it is today (again - fees for 3 uniswap swaps pay for it). You can even buy 8tb for $830 today. The bandwidth in particular, in any developed city a mobile phone gets 600Mbps on LTE+, and 5g is being deployed everywhere.
>You might get it in the richest part of the biggest city
People living elsewhere are extremely unlikely to even afford fees, so that's limiting throughput to everyone for nonexisting user. At worst it's a temporary situation as network speeds increase globally due to starlink and this argument becomes a complete non-issue.
>If people really want gas prices to go down I think the right solution is to support/fund/work on:
the issue is that there's no time for that. BSC already hit 8M daily tx. Network effects are nonlinear.
Weirdly, this is a very close repeat of the bitcoin situation where ln was the supposed answer to any scalability problems, with people dead certain that adoption is going to stay with bitcoin, but what instead happened is that people moved elsewhere, mostly to ethereum.

Would you still support not increasing gas limits, knowing for a certainty that it means that in 2023, ethereum is mostly unused - about 200k tx/day, nobody uses rollups, market cap is out of top 10, and all action happens on centralized blockchains?
